rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 1 (sensor x = -0.04..+0.04, size 0.012, kp 3.0, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.4) is still the best raced design at 154.1. Iteration 2 (kp 3.5) showed kp is not the lever for line loss, and it fell to 125.8. Iteration 3 (sensor_size 0.016, otherwise identical to iteration 1) scored 149.8. Its line loss did not fall where it matters: s-bend 1.05 and slalom 1.00 per run, against 1.00 and 1.00 in iteration 1. Only the oval improved (0.85 line-loss events, 2 finishes in 20). Line loss is still near 1.0 on every track, so the footprint is not the cause. Oscillation stayed in the 0.11 to 0.30 range, so the controller is not unstable.

Change. Following the Evaluator's rule (b), I return sensor_size to 0.012 and narrow the sensor spread to x = -0.03, -0.015, 0.0, 0.015, 0.03 at y = 0.03. This is the only geometry change from iteration 1. kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.4, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] and line_loss last_direction are unchanged, so the effect of the spread can be read cleanly.

Hypotheses. (a) A narrower spread keeps the 25 mm tape under at least one sensor more often on the tighter bends, so line-loss events fall below about 0.9 per run. (b) If line loss stays at 1.0, the cause is turn-in lag rather than sensing coverage, and the next lever is kd or a forward sensor offset. Expected result: score near or above 154, with progress on the s-bend and slalom at least as high as iteration 1. Risk: the narrower spread is closer to iteration 0 (which scored 117 at x = -0.02..+0.02), so this may score lower. If so, the next step is to keep the iteration-1 spread and test kd 0.3 to 0.4.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track, so I can separate the spread effect from speed and damping.
